1.0.10 (build 4207)   Nov 14, 2026   This version

New

  • A Viewer's view splits in two (its split button or chip menu): each side shows another Viewer or another input of the same Viewer, in 2D or 3D on its own, kept with the layout.
  • In a split Viewer, the Scopes, the Pixel inspector and the Flipbook follow the side you clicked last, its own input too; on a side showing the 3D they say so in words.
  • The Lens node's Stills lenses is one window, not menus on menus: type to find a lens, the plate's camera already chosen, the focal lengths as a row of choices.
  • The Timeline's frame strip takes all the width the controls leave: in and out sit at its ends, the save status is a dot (hover for its words) and the rate as played shows in the strip's corner.
  • Inference has a mask input and mix: connect a roto to keep a model's change inside it, as a Trainer fix should be.
  • An assistant connected to Kento can ask what the studio's artists usually wire after a node and how they set it. Each answer says how many shots it rests on and how those shots went in Kitsu.
  • In a Timeline narrower than 1,400 points, Marks, Client notes and the volume move into the playback pop-up and the timecode into the frame field's tip, so the frame strip is about a quarter wider (590 to 745 points in the Compositing layout on a 1,728-point window).
  • Floating Viewer windows are kept with the layout: Kento opens them again where they were, at their size, in 2D or 3D, each on its Viewer.
  • The Trainer's Out has Make an Inference node: the active pass as an Inference node of its own beside the Trainer, its mask wired to the Trainer's, so the fix can be used without the Trainer.
  • A light chooses which objects cast its shadow: Blocked by on its Shadows tab (Every object, Only the chosen, All but the chosen, with Choose's checks), and on its row in the Scene panel. An object left out still casts the other lights' shadows.
  • The Scene panel shows each object's Cast, Receive and Catcher as three small columns beside its eyes: click to turn one on or off, on every selected object at once.

Fixed

  • A render that fails above the Viewer (a plug-in's render error such as kOfxStatErrBadHandle, an expression's mistake) is no longer a silent black: the Viewer's corner names the node and why, a card by the node gives the fix (Try again for a plug-in), and the node lights red.
  • Photoshop files in a .nk comp read as they did in the comp: a layer's mask is its own channel (layer.mask), its alpha the layer's transparency alone, the flattened picture's clear areas as the file stores them, and a layer named RGB or main keeps its own channels.
  • IBKColour fills right out to where its blur reaches: on a bright plate its last pixels had come out black.
  • In a comp using Nuke's own color management, a Read of an EXR in sRGB, rec709, Cineon or another of Nuke's LUTs holds values past 1 at the LUT's top, as the comp did before it came to Kento, instead of stretching them.
  • A Crop box at half pixels rounds a half to the even pixel, so a .nk comp's reformatted Crop keeps the size it had.
  • Every data pass shows readably in the Viewer by itself, however you get to it: an image with only a depth or motion pass shows it at once, ID passes (objectId, matId) show a color per object, normals can be lit by a light you turn on a small sphere, motion shows its direction wheel, and values outside near and far are striped dark red instead of clipped to black or white. The info bar always says the range shown (for depth, the frame's own nearest to farthest).
  • The Trainer learns a small fix such as a paint-out: most passes used to come out unchanged from the plate. Limit to mask is now on by default.
  • With where it's fixed set to The mask input, the Trainer keeps its fix inside the mask: the plate outside it is left exactly as it was.
  • ScanlineRender's Passes tab is complete and its layer pictures are the right way up: Darken the plate under it is a button again (dim, with the reason under it, until there is a plate), the pictures fit a narrow panel and say when a pass is off, and Reach and Contact shadows have their notes.
  • A ScanlineRender's depth is listed once, as the depth layer under Data, not also among rgba's channels: choosing it shows the depth in gray between its own near and far, near bright.
  • Two Viewers side by side keep their own 2D or 3D: switching one to the 3D view no longer switches the other, docked or floating, and the layout remembers which views show the 3D.
  • A view whose Viewer is in another view no longer refuses to float in silence: the float button and the chip dragged out say why by the control, with a button that closes the other view and floats this one.
  • Perspective on a long lens says the lines can't measure the focal, where it blamed a line on the wrong axis; the new Solve from choice "two axes, focal typed" makes the camera from a typed focal.
  • The Lens node's Work it out from lines measures a wide lens's distortion: an 18 mm lens comes back within a pixel at the frame's corner, where it was 248 px out, and gentler lenses that went unnoticed are found.
  • Perspective no longer makes a confidently wrong camera when one direction's lines are wrong (a 40 mm plate solved as 259 mm): it solves from the other two, or says why it can't.
  • Perspective's From the pictures lines up two plates of one wall or sign shot from far apart (turned, nearer, at a slant) by the features they share, and says why when it can't, instead of making a corner pin hundreds of pixels off.
  • Long frame numbers, such as eight-digit timecode frames, show every digit in the Timeline's start, end and frame fields and the ruler's numbers no longer run into each other; the fields are sized with the range, so nothing on the line moves while it plays.
  • Clicking in the Viewer where a Roto shape is that isn't alive at this frame, or has its visibility off, no longer does nothing: a card says which shape and why ("Shape3 isn't alive at frame 1040", its life 1001 to 1030), with Extend its life to here or Make it visible as the fix.
  • A .nk comp on Nuke 17's ACES 2.0 configs (fn-nuke_cg-config-v3.0.0 and the studio one) uses that config, so its Reads' default color spaces (matte_paint, texture_paint, compositing_log) are the comp's own.
  • A one-channel picture (a gray PNG, TIFF or JPEG) reads into red and is converted like red, as the comp had it, instead of an unconverted other.Y.
  • LightKey's Screen PreBlur and the tuning gains (Shadow, Midtones and Highlights Gain, Mid Tones At) now work, Clip Rollback works (closely from 2 pixels up, roughly below), and Alpha Bias and Despill Bias key off-gray screens as the original does on a green screen.
  • LightKey's Source Alpha Handling now works: Normal keys only where the source's alpha is, and Add To Inside Mask adds the source's alpha to the inside mask (both had been taken as Ignore).

Faster

  • The processing glow on the Node Graph steps more coarsely the bigger the comp, and on a comp too big to pulse without slowing the interface it glows steady instead.
  • Playback from a full cache keeps its pace: a 24 fps comp plays at 24, where it ran at about 18.
  • A big comp settles sooner after it opens: the menus are no longer built a second time (about 2 seconds on a large comp).
  • After a big comp opens, its Node Graph no longer redraws itself over and over (about a quarter as many redraws on an 11,000-node comp); only the processing glow pulses in coarser steps there.
  • Heavy 4K comps render faster, the same picture: a 3D scene of textured cards with motion blur about a quarter faster, and frames with Bokeh or LightKey about a fifth faster, on a 16 GB Mac.
  • Erode (filter) with a large size renders several times faster, the same picture: a 4K frame with a Gaussian grow of 200 renders a third faster on a 16 GB Mac.
  • Convolve renders about 25 times faster: a comp with a lens-defocus gizmo built on Convolve renders in minutes, where one shot took over 8 hours.
  • NoTimeBlur keeps a TimeBlur's sub-frames from everything above it, with any rounding: those nodes see the whole frame and are worked out once a frame, where they were sampled at each sub-frame (rounding none) or at two frames (floor, rint, ceil).
  • Convolve no longer darkens a plate toward its edges: past the input's box it repeats the edge pixels, where it read black (up to 0.32 off with a 41-pixel disc).
  • Comps with a TimeBlur render faster and in far less memory: parts of the comp that don't change between its sub-frames are worked out once (a whole shot in 18 minutes and 16 GB, where its last frame alone stalled for over 20 minutes).
  • Moving objects in the 3D view is smoother in every draw mode: a sphere's wireframe is no longer rebuilt and the comp's insides are no longer searched at each step of the drag. With the render shown in a Viewer beside it, the drag stays smooth too: the Viewer holds its picture while you drag, catches up when you pause, and shows the result when you let go (a step about 200 ms to 60-120 ms). Every Python expression also runs faster, compiled once instead of at every run.
  • MotionBlur works out its motion faster, the same picture: on a 16 GB Mac its motion vectors take about a quarter less time at 2K and a fifth less at 4K; VectorGenerator gains too.
  • VectorRetime renders about 40 percent faster at 4K and 30 percent at 2K on a 16 GB Mac, the same picture: its warps no longer carry the motion vectors along.
  • VectorGenerator with confidence on and VectorRetime with blend if unsure render in Kento's own render engine, the same picture as before.
  • Dragging an object in the 3D view is about twice as quick again (a step about 70 ms to 35 in Wire, 95 to 45 in Lit), with the Node Graph waiting until you pause. In Lit, the dragged object's surface now moves with it, where it stayed behind until you let go; Shaded, Textured and Lit draw at half detail while you drag and in full when you let go.
  • A big comp's window freezes less just after it opens: the Shot panel no longer holds it while it lists the shot (it says "Looking up the shot..." until the list comes), and its Node Graph redraws less in its first second; the longest freeze on a 16 GB Mac is about 0.7 seconds, where it was often over 1.
  • Bokeh and ZDefocus render their depth layers about a quarter faster, and a 3D scene of cards flattens faster, the same picture.

1.0.9 (build 4076)   Nov 12, 2026

New

  • Local renders: Kura Writes can render to a fast drive on your machine and copy each frame to the Suite drive behind you, carrying on after Kento closes. Turn it on in Settings, Shot and studio (the same switch as the Nuke Shot panel's). Nobody can see your render, unless it is uploaded.
  • Send to Dailies waits until the Suite server has every frame, then goes by itself; tick "send to dailies once it's on Suite" on a Kura Write to send each render that way.
  • Pen-friendly zoom and pan, the same in the Viewer, Node Graph, Curve Editor and Dope Sheet: hold Z and drag to zoom about where you start, hold Space and drag to pan; a tap still does what the key did.
  • Segment Anything's Cattery gizmo works in Kento, matching NukeX's mattes.
  • A .nk script you import with a CopyCat node in it brings that node in as a Trainer, with its settings and frames.
  • The Scene panel is an outliner of what's in the scene: each object, light and camera by the node that makes it, with eyes to leave one out of the render, each render's camera chosen from a menu, and what's wrong said in plain words with its fix.
  • Lens: pick a stills lens from Lensfun's database by the plate's camera and maker; its calibration comes in exactly, and a zoom's terms follow each frame's focal length. OpenCV's full model and a radial polynomial join the lens models.
  • Shortcuts here: hold ? over any panel to see its keys, grouped by what you're doing, with the window's and the menus' beside them; tap ? and the card stays open. Its search finds a key or what it does in every panel, and keys you changed show as yours.
  • Cattery models in the node menu: Other, Models lists the Trainer, Inference and every Cattery model by what it does (depth, segmentation, flow), each with a line on what it's for; Tab search finds them too.
  • The Trainer without wiring: pick the node that holds your fixes from a menu (or paint a fix), each frame pair is checked with numbers before training (offset, exposure, how much changed), training crops are drawn in the Viewer, and a pass's checkpoints can be browsed with a picture and their scores, and one chosen.
  • Soft shadows in 3D: a light's size softens its shadow, sharp where an object touches the ground and softer further away, with a preview of the soft edge on the light's Shadows tab; point lights cast shadows too. ScanlineRender's Passes tab adds the shadow on the plate and ambient occlusion as layers, and a Card or other object can be a shadow catcher, hidden in the beauty if you like.
  • Light linking: a light's Lights menu lights every object, only the chosen or all but the chosen, picked with checks on its Shadows tab or in the Scene panel (Lit by on an object's ... menu). The Scene panel's rows also show shadow catchers and soft lights, and their ... menus set Cast shadow, Receive shadow and Shadow catcher on every selected object at once.
  • Darken the plate under it, on ScanlineRender's Passes tab: one click adds the shadow layer's multiply over the plate (a Merge whose mix is the strength), after the render or under the CG, one undo. The tab also shows thumbnails of the beauty, shadow and occlusion layers from the frame the Viewer shows.
  • Shadows in the 3D view: with Lit, a Shadows check draws each light's shadows as the render does, worked out in the background, and a soft light shows its size as a ring. A light's shadow Mode can now be Clipped alpha or Full alpha, so a card casts the shape of its texture's alpha. Soft shadows render faster, and the shadow layer no longer traces its rays a second time on a lit catcher.

Better

  • Perspective matching settles on the same answer from any reasonable start on real plates, and a lens it can't measure is left alone rather than bent.
  • Boxes through a comp match NukeX's in more places: a Transform sees through disabled nodes, a Reformat by scale rounds as NukeX does, and a large Blur's box is the right size.
  • Retime and TimeWarp over a Read give the same frames as NukeX in every frame mode, and VectorRetime's Frame timing can reach past the input's range.
  • MotionBlur leaves the plate untouched at very short shutters, as NukeX does.
  • The playback cache keeps its frames through a save and anything else that doesn't change the picture.
  • Kiri on a blue screen finds the blue by itself (it looked for green until a color was picked), and its edges hold steady from frame to frame where the plate doesn't move.
  • Until you pick a screen color, Kiri finds it in the plate at every frame, including a screen with two shades, such as a stage's wall and floor.
  • SmartMerge finds skin on every skin tone, and Kiri's Match to background matches the plate's color from skin first, then the mid-tones near the subject.
  • A tag cut short in Properties keeps the mark that takes it off.
  • The manual names nodes as you know them (Merge, Tracker, CornerPin) and describes Kento in its own terms.

Faster

  • Heavy 4K comps render much faster on Macs with 16 GB: a BOU_120 frame in about 5.3 seconds on a Mac mini, where it took 11 to 20, using a third of the memory, and RAI_120's wide soft Erode (a dilate of 200) in 3.1 seconds where it took 6.9, with exactly the same pixels.
  • Big comps open faster: a 4K show comp with hundreds of Reads in about 9 seconds on a 16 GB Mac mini, where it took 17. An edit just after it shows no longer waits for a thumbnail to read its plate.
  • Dragging many selected nodes stays smooth: 30 frames a second with 500 nodes on a 16 GB Mac mini, and 49 with 300.
  • MotionBlur at 4K is about a fifth faster, and optical flow can run on the GPU.
  • RotoPaint's strokes render up to 2.4 times faster at 4K (a 16 GB Mac mini), with the same pixels; a 3D render's merges and deep flattening use about half the time they did.

Fixed

  • A save no longer empties the playback cache.
  • Track backwards and the tracker's other keys reach the Tracker in the Viewer.
  • Cattery models with half-precision weights work out right when run on the processor (Segment Anything's matte was empty).
  • Zoomed far out in the Node Graph, pressing a node near its connectors moves it, rather than starting a wire; a wire starts from the connector's ring beside the node.

  • Local renders: Kura Writes can render to a fast drive on your machine and copy each frame to the Suite drive behind you, carrying on after Kento closes. Turn it on in Settings, Shot and studio (the same switch as the Nuke Shot panel's). Nobody can see your render, unless it is uploaded.
  • Send to Dailies waits until the Suite server has every frame, then goes by itself; tick "send to dailies once it's on Suite" on a Kura Write to send each render that way.
  • Pen-friendly zoom and pan, the same in the Viewer, Node Graph, Curve Editor and Dope Sheet: hold Z and drag to zoom about where you start, hold Space and drag to pan; a tap still does what the key did.
  • Segment Anything's Cattery gizmo works in Kento, matching NukeX's mattes.
  • A .nk script you import with a CopyCat node in it brings that node in as a Trainer, with its settings and frames.
  • The Scene panel is an outliner of what's in the scene: each object, light and camera by the node that makes it, with eyes to leave one out of the render, each render's camera chosen from a menu, and what's wrong said in plain words with its fix.
  • Lens: pick a stills lens from Lensfun's database by the plate's camera and maker; its calibration comes in exactly, and a zoom's terms follow each frame's focal length. OpenCV's full model and a radial polynomial join the lens models.
  • Shortcuts here: hold ? over any panel to see its keys, grouped by what you're doing, with the window's and the menus' beside them; tap ? and the card stays open. Its search finds a key or what it does in every panel, and keys you changed show as yours.
  • Cattery models in the node menu: Other, Models lists the Trainer, Inference and every Cattery model by what it does (depth, segmentation, flow), each with a line on what it's for; Tab search finds them too.
  • The Trainer without wiring: pick the node that holds your fixes from a menu (or paint a fix), each frame pair is checked with numbers before training (offset, exposure, how much changed), training crops are drawn in the Viewer, and a pass's checkpoints can be browsed with a picture and their scores, and one chosen.
  • Soft shadows in 3D: a light's size softens its shadow, sharp where an object touches the ground and softer further away, with a preview of the soft edge on the light's Shadows tab; point lights cast shadows too. ScanlineRender's Passes tab adds the shadow on the plate and ambient occlusion as layers, and a Card or other object can be a shadow catcher, hidden in the beauty if you like.
  • Light linking: a light's Lights menu lights every object, only the chosen or all but the chosen, picked with checks on its Shadows tab or in the Scene panel (Lit by on an object's ... menu). The Scene panel's rows also show shadow catchers and soft lights, and their ... menus set Cast shadow, Receive shadow and Shadow catcher on every selected object at once.
  • Darken the plate under it, on ScanlineRender's Passes tab: one click adds the shadow layer's multiply over the plate (a Merge whose mix is the strength), after the render or under the CG, one undo. The tab also shows thumbnails of the beauty, shadow and occlusion layers from the frame the Viewer shows.
  • Shadows in the 3D view: with Lit, a Shadows check draws each light's shadows as the render does, worked out in the background, and a soft light shows its size as a ring. A light's shadow Mode can now be Clipped alpha or Full alpha, so a card casts the shape of its texture's alpha. Soft shadows render faster, and the shadow layer no longer traces its rays a second time on a lit catcher.

Better

  • Perspective matching settles on the same answer from any reasonable start on real plates, and a lens it can't measure is left alone rather than bent.
  • Boxes through a comp match NukeX's in more places: a Transform sees through disabled nodes, a Reformat by scale rounds as NukeX does, and a large Blur's box is the right size.
  • Retime and TimeWarp over a Read give the same frames as NukeX in every frame mode, and VectorRetime's Frame timing can reach past the input's range.
  • MotionBlur leaves the plate untouched at very short shutters, as NukeX does.
  • The playback cache keeps its frames through a save and anything else that doesn't change the picture.
  • Kiri on a blue screen finds the blue by itself (it looked for green until a color was picked), and its edges hold steady from frame to frame where the plate doesn't move.
  • Until you pick a screen color, Kiri finds it in the plate at every frame, including a screen with two shades, such as a stage's wall and floor.
  • SmartMerge finds skin on every skin tone, and Kiri's Match to background matches the plate's color from skin first, then the mid-tones near the subject.
  • A tag cut short in Properties keeps the mark that takes it off.
  • The manual names nodes as you know them (Merge, Tracker, CornerPin) and describes Kento in its own terms.

Faster

  • Heavy 4K comps render much faster on Macs with 16 GB: a BOU_120 frame in about 5.3 seconds on a Mac mini, where it took 11 to 20, using a third of the memory, and RAI_120's wide soft Erode (a dilate of 200) in 3.1 seconds where it took 6.9, with exactly the same pixels.
  • Big comps open faster: a 4K show comp with hundreds of Reads in about 9 seconds on a 16 GB Mac mini, where it took 17. An edit just after it shows no longer waits for a thumbnail to read its plate.
  • Dragging many selected nodes stays smooth: 30 frames a second with 500 nodes on a 16 GB Mac mini, and 49 with 300.
  • MotionBlur at 4K is about a fifth faster, and optical flow can run on the GPU.
  • RotoPaint's strokes render up to 2.4 times faster at 4K (a 16 GB Mac mini), with the same pixels; a 3D render's merges and deep flattening use about half the time they did.

Fixed

  • A save no longer empties the playback cache.
  • Track backwards and the tracker's other keys reach the Tracker in the Viewer.
  • Cattery models with half-precision weights work out right when run on the processor (Segment Anything's matte was empty).
  • Zoomed far out in the Node Graph, pressing a node near its connectors moves it, rather than starting a wire; a wire starts from the connector's ring beside the node.
1.0.8 (build 3923)   Nov 12, 2026

New

  • CameraTracker shows how well a solve covers the shot and how closely it fits, before you export it.
  • Lens imports rectilinear calibrations from Lensfun (poly5) exactly.
  • Cattery models run in Kento: a gizmo built on a .cat (DepthPro, Depth Anything and the like) works out its picture on the GPU, frame by frame or the whole shot in the background, from your Cattery folders (Settings, AI and MCP). A missing model says which gizmo needs it and lets you find it.
  • A node switched off by an expression shows it on its tile, and the node that makes the picture's box grow is marked.
  • Chroma Rebuild smooths a 4:2:0 or 4:2:2 movie's color before keying, reading the movie's subsampling and color matrix from its Read; older comps keep the way they worked.

Faster

  • Opening a big comp: a 4K show comp with hundreds of Reads opens in about 16 seconds on a 16 GB Mac mini (5 on a Mac Studio, where it took 40).
  • STMap on the CPU is about 1.6 times faster at 4K.

Fixed

  • Adding a node while the Viewer's input process is on no longer freezes Kento.
  • A Read whose file is on only one of the studio drive's mounts (Autonomy or laxnas) reads it from the one that has it; when neither has it, the error names both.
  • RotoPaint's eraser and reveal over a plate without alpha leave alpha where they paint, as Nuke does (comps over such plates had holes in their alpha).
  • ZDefocus no longer turns plates without alpha into extreme bright pixels (BOU_180's background), and near depths over such plates blend as in Nuke.
  • Long renders no longer stop when the disk cache fills: a decoded frame still in use isn't cleared.
  • Notes in a .nk imported into an open comp are laid out at once; a group's inner nodes with no position in the .nk are saved back without one, so Nuke lays them out.
  • With the Viewer set to a smaller size, a picture cropped with an expression such as width or height (inside depth tools, for example) no longer shrinks to a quarter of the frame.
  • Optimize no longer says "Couldn't measure this frame" on comps holding MergeExpression, Convolve, LiveGroupInfo, ModifyMetaData or the vector retime nodes.
  • The render command line no longer crashes after it has written its frames.
  • A Read's color tag shows again on the narrower tiles.
  • Colorspace uses the right white points when converting between spaces.
  • Retime keeps the transforms chained after it, sampled on the right frames.
  • Crop's autocrop rounds its box the way Nuke does.
  • Card lattices are the right size with a lens in front.
  • CameraTracker's No Lens Distortion setting is kept.
  • PSD files with two layers of the same name open with both layers.
  • Vector maps carried through warps keep the right values and windows.
  • Kiri: mattes whose freshness record is missing or damaged are marked out of date; background keying keeps the comp it started from.

1.0.7 (build 3786)   Nov 11, 2026

New

  • The Node Graph's tiles are 112 px wide, so trees are more compact; zoomed out, a name can run past its tile's end rather than be cut, and long names shorten in the middle with the full name on hover.
  • 3D nodes are told apart at a glance: cameras end in a lens, lights in a small sun, Scene in a cube, ball and cone, and Axis in three arrows.
  • A node with a warning is edged and banded in hatched yellow, and a node's own color tints the whole tile with a wide stripe at its left, easy to see from a distance.
  • Blender 5.3 works with CameraTracker's Blender solve and 3D file conversions; 5.2 still does.
  • Denoise2 has a second method, OpenImageDenoise, with optional Albedo and Normal inputs for cleaner detail. It runs on the CPU or Metal. Existing comps keep Nagi.
  • ScanlineRender can cast solid shadows from directional and spot lights. Turn on Cast shadows in the light's Shadows tab.
  • VectorRetime has a Matte input and separate Foreground and Background outputs.
  • Roto has an Edge time-strip window that shows how a shape's edge slips, chatters or drifts across the shot.
  • CameraTracker: lasso solved tracks in the Viewer to delete the outliers; focal length and lens distortion come back from Blender solves.
  • GridWarp can follow a PlanarTracker, with live links or baked keys.
  • Arrange has Grid size and Grid dots sliders and a compact tree layout that keeps branches readable.
  • What's New in the Kento menu (Help menu on Windows) opens a searchable history of every release's notes, offline.
  • Lens: Brown-Conrady, equidistant fisheye, and the 3DEqualizer Classic LD and Radial Standard models; CameraTracker now keeps the full Lens model when you hand it a calibration.
  • Tab search puts the nodes you most often wire after the selected one first.
  • Write can save a full-frame padded display window and a single-channel grayscale matte for client deliveries, without touching working color.
  • Curve groups keep live motions such as Chaos and Lag instead of baking them to keys.
  • Studio scripts get the Kento Python module, with progress dialogs and a built-in reference.

Faster

  • STMap on the CPU is about 1.6 times faster at 4K.
  • Large blurs run on Metal: about 2.3 times faster for a 4K, radius 100 blur.
  • Big RotoPaint strokes are calculated in parallel: up to 3 times faster at 4K.
  • Nodes that leave a plane unchanged share it instead of copying it: repeat renders of 4K comps are 9 to 14 percent faster.
  • Selecting hundreds of nodes is quick again, and Tidy no longer stalls on large comps.
  • Viewers hidden behind other panels stop rendering and reading ahead, so background CPU use drops from several cores to almost nothing.
  • Reading a frame again right after it was read is about 2.7 times faster (decoded tiles stay in memory when idle files close).
  • Checking that files exist no longer freezes the interface during playback and scrubbing.

Fixed

  • Paths written as a drive with its slash left out (X:kura/...) map like X:/kura instead of being read next to the comp.
  • Importing a gizmo as a Bento no longer fails.
  • Zoomed all the way in, a tile is still over 500 px wide.
  • CameraTracker: Blender solves line up with your plate's frame numbers, keep coordinates right on anamorphic plates, and use your latest mesh after you re-export geometry.
  • Kiri: Stop ends a stuck model process; changing a model setting marks old mattes out of date; keying stops with a message when the input sequence is incomplete; color picks no longer overwrite protected samples; a bad hair result keeps your previous matte instead of publishing it.
  • Comps from studio scripts keep their Tracker4 row selection.
  • ScanlineRender keeps an OBJ's own vertex normals when lit.
  • 3D handles draw and drag in the object's parent frame, not world axes.
  • In focus mode, selecting an already selected node or box-selecting no longer opens Properties; only an explicit click does.
  • Tab search no longer connects a wire of the wrong kind, and never reroutes an existing output.
  • VectorDistort only warps the channels you chose.
  • Camera2, Axis2, Mirror2 and LiveGroupInfo have descriptions and Help pages.
  • Remote control reports who is busy, queues overlapping requests, and approval prompts no longer block it.
  • Settings label a comp's own value "this comp only".

Windows

  • An interface scale option in Settings, kept across restarts.
  • The file browser keeps drive letters and network share names in its path bar.
  • Color pickers close with their panel without crashing.
  • Paths over 260 characters work in the launcher, the installed runtime and the movie tools.
  • Roto curves with quotes save and reopen correctly; Roto edge rounding matches the Mac.
  • The Viewer shows reliably when a panel opens; toolbars close without errors.
  • Help stays the last menu; render queue jobs keep their destination folders; the launcher says which runtime file is missing or why a child process failed.
